overview.title: 📖 Overview: The Limits of Partial Consecration
overview.subtitle: Temurah 11a–11b
overview.hebrewSource: רַגְלָהּ שֶׁל זוֹ עוֹלָה — כּוּלָּהּ עוֹלָה
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: The daf finishes the bar Padda–Rabbi Yoḥanan dispute over fetal sanctity, narrowing their true disagreement to an unblemished fetus inside a blemished mother. A new thread opens with Rabbi Eliezer's list of animals — hybrids, a tereifa, one born by caesarean, a tumtum, a hermaphrodite — that are 'neither sacred nor sanctify,' sharpened by Shmuel to mean specifically that they cannot serve as or receive a substitute. The mishna's other dispute, between Rabbi Yosei and the Rabbis over whether consecrating a single limb sanctifies the whole animal, is traced to competing readings of Leviticus 27:9. The daf closes with a cluster of Rava's dilemmas — about birds, and about a limb consecrated purely for its value — and a practical discussion with Abaye about shearing wool or working an animal only partially consecrated.

slides.title: 🫀 Rabbi Zeira's Last Defense: Vital Organs
slides.subtitle: Even a die-hard defense of bar Padda has its limits

nodes.content: ❓ R' Yirmeya: if this mishna follows Rabbi Yehuda, doesn't Rabbi Yehuda deny that consecrating a leg sanctifies the whole animal? Then how can consecrated limbs ever spread sanctity?
💬 R' Zeira: we're speaking here of a limb whose removal would make the animal a tereifa (fatally injured) — even Rabbi Yehuda concedes THIS extends to the whole animal
✅ Bar Padda's position survives: ordinary limbs don't spread sanctity (per R' Yehuda), but vital, life-sustaining limbs do

callout.label: Narrowed dispute:
callout.text: Ultimately Abaye pins the bar Padda/R' Yoḥanan dispute down to one precise case: an unblemished fetus inside a blemished mother — is the fetus a separate 'body' that can still receive inherent sanctity?

slides.title: 🐐 Rabbi Eliezer's List: Which Animals Can't Be Sacred?
slides.subtitle: Kilayim, tereifa, yotzei dofen, tumtum, and androginos
rows: Hybrid (kilayim), tereifa, born by caesarean, tumtum, hermaphrodite
Specifically: cannot become, or generate, a valid substitute (temurah)
Same animal, consecrated then it became one of these
Rabbi Meir: CAN be sacred in this order
Proves a fetus can be consecrated — challenging bar Padda
Unblemished fetus in an unblemished mother's womb
Unblemished fetus in a blemished mother's womb
Bar Padda: not consecrated (follows mother's status)
Rabbi Yoḥanan: fetus is a separate 'body,' still consecrated

callout.label: Bottom line:
callout.text: The real bar Padda/Rabbi Yoḥanan dispute narrows to whether a fetus's sanctity can exceed its mother's.

slides.title: 🦵 Does Consecrating One Leg Sanctify the Whole Animal?
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon vs. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda

lines.speaker: R' Yosei/Shimon
lines.text: 'All that any man gives of it to the Lord shall be sacred' (Lev. 27:9) — the extra phrase 'shall be sacred' includes the ENTIRE animal, not just the limb given.

lines.speaker: R' Meir/Yehuda
lines.text: No — 'anything OF IT that one gives to the Lord, it shall be sacred' — only the part actually given is sacred, 'of it,' not all of it.

lines.speaker: Practical outcome
lines.text: For R' Meir/Yehuda: the animal is sold to fund burnt offerings, with all proceeds non-sacred except the value attributable to the consecrated limb.

lines.speaker: Rava clarifies
lines.text: That sale works only to a buyer who vowed to bring a burnt offering using only the animal's vital limbs — since the consecrated limb need not be among them, the sale isn't invalidated.

callout.label: Underlying agreement:
callout.text: Even Rabbi Yehuda concedes that consecrating a limb whose removal would kill the animal (or make it a tereifa/neveila) DOES spread sanctity to the whole body.

slides.title: ❓ Rava's Chain of Unresolved Dilemmas
slides.subtitle: Each new case tests how far 'one limb sanctifies all' can be pushed

steps.content: 1️⃣ A bird fit for sacrifice: does Rabbi Yosei's rule (verse says 'behema,' an animal) apply, or does 'korban' cover it too? — Teiku
2️⃣ One consecrates a limb purely for its value (not as an offering): does inherent sanctity (kedushat haguf) spread to the whole animal too, layering two expansions at once? — Teiku
3️⃣ Attempted resolution: Rava elsewhere says consecrating a male animal 'for its value' still gives it inherent sanctity automatically — so shouldn't a single limb work the same way?
4️⃣ Rejected: consecrating the WHOLE animal for value is different from consecrating just ONE limb for value — the dilemma stands

callout.label: Pattern:
callout.text: Rava repeatedly probes the outer edge of 'partial consecration spreading further' — and repeatedly the Gemara leaves the answer open.

slides.title: 🐑 How Far Does Partial Consecration Restrict the Animal?
slides.subtitle: Abaye questions Rava about shearing wool and using the animal for labor

boxes.title: Shearing (Gizah)
items: One limb consecrated (R' Yehuda: sanctity doesn't spread)
Rava: compare to a jointly-owned firstborn, which may be sheared
Rejected — here sanctity DID take hold on that limb, unlike a gentile-owned share

boxes.title: Labor (Avoda)
items: Consecrating only the skin — may the animal still work?
Compared to a consecrated fetus: mother may be sheared but not worked (labor weakens/reduces value)
Abaye: is that prohibition Torah law or rabbinic?
Rava: only rabbinic — shearing (non-weakening) was never restricted, but labor (weakening) was

callout.label: Underlying logic:
callout.text: The Sages restrict activities that would actively diminish the value of the consecrated part, even by rabbinic decree, while permitting those that don't.

summary.principle: Consecration of a fetus, or of a single limb, spreads only under specific conditions — a vital organ extends sanctity to the whole body, while ordinary limbs and a fetus inside a blemished mother remain genuinely disputed or limited to value-sanctity alone.

flowSteps.content: 🫀 Bar Padda's position survives: vital limbs (tereifa-causing) spread sanctity; ordinary ones don't
🐐 R' Eliezer: hybrids, tereifot, tumtum, androginos can't be substitutes; dispute narrows to fetus-in-blemished-mother

columns.content: 🦵 R' Yosei: one leg sanctifies the whole animal; Rabbis: only the leg itself
🐑 Sages restrict activities (labor) that reduce a consecrated part's value

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: sanctity's reach depends on whether the consecrated part is vital to the whole body

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Zeira's final answer, which limbs does even Rabbi Yehuda concede spread sanctity to the entire animal?
o: Any limb whatsoever
Only limbs whose removal would render the animal a tereifa (vital organs)
Only the legs
No limbs — Rabbi Yehuda never concedes
quiz.e: Rabbi Zeira explains that Rabbi Yehuda's rule that limb-consecration doesn't spread applies only to non-vital limbs; for a limb whose removal would make the animal a tereifa, even Rabbi Yehuda agrees the sanctity extends throughout.

quiz.q: According to the discussion of Rabbi Eliezer's list (kilayim, tereifa, tumtum, androginos, etc.), how does Shmuel explain 'neither sacred nor sanctify'?
o: These animals can never be eaten
They cannot become a substitute, nor can a substitute be made for them
They are automatically non-sacred forever
They can only be sacrificed as guilt offerings
quiz.e: Shmuel clarifies that Rabbi Eliezer's statement is specifically about temurah: these animals cannot serve as, or receive, a valid substitute — not that they can never have any sanctity at all.

quiz.q: After the extended debate, to what specific case does the bar Padda/Rabbi Yoḥanan dispute ultimately narrow?
o: Whether any animal at all can be consecrated
An unblemished fetus in the womb of a blemished mother
Whether priests can consecrate animals
Whether temurah applies to birds
quiz.e: Abaye clarifies that everyone agrees an unblemished fetus in an unblemished mother is consecrated; the true dispute is only about an unblemished fetus inside a blemished mother, where bar Padda ties the fetus's status to its mother's and Rabbi Yoḥanan treats it as a separate body.

quiz.q: According to Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon, what verse teaches that consecrating one limb sanctifies the entire animal?
o: "He shall not exchange it"
"All that any man gives of it to the Lord SHALL BE SACRED" (Lev. 27:9) — the extra phrase includes the whole animal
"Both it and its substitute shall be holy"
There is no verse; it's pure logic
quiz.e: Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon read the seemingly redundant phrase 'shall be sacred' in Leviticus 27:9 as expanding the consecration to the entire animal, not merely the limb explicitly given.

quiz.q: According to Rava's explanation to Abaye, why is it prohibited (by rabbinic law) to use for labor an animal whose fetus alone was consecrated, while shearing it remains permitted?
o: Both are equally forbidden by Torah law
Labor weakens the animal and reduces the fetus's value, which the Sages decreed against; shearing doesn't weaken it, so it was never restricted
Shearing is always forbidden for any consecrated item
There is no difference between the two activities
quiz.e: Rava explains the Sages specifically prohibited activities like labor that actively diminish value through weakening, while non-weakening activities like shearing were left permitted.
